name: Posteromedial approach to the tibial shaft
corridor: Incision 1–2 cm posterior to the posteromedial tibial border, saphenous structures taken anteriorly, then extra-periosteal mobilization of the superficial and deep posterior compartments to the posterolateral tibial edge

positioning.text: Position supine with the knee flexed and the hip externally rotated, or prone, which needs less manipulation.

surface_landmarks.text: Palpate the posteromedial tibial border along its length and mark a line 1–2 cm posterior to it. Note the saphenous vein and nerve.

incision.text: Incise parallel to and 1–2 cm behind the posterior tibial border. Length follows the fracture and plate. Mini-open cuts are safe in this region.

superficial_interval.text: Identify and protect the saphenous vein and nerve and typically mobilize them anteriorly.

deep_interval.text: Incise fascia in line with the skin and mobilize the superficial and deep posterior compartments. Gastrocnemius, soleus, and flexor digitorum are lifted extra-periosteally according to fracture level. Do not dissect beyond the posterolateral tibial edge. The middle three-fifths of the posterior tibia can be shown. The fibula is not reached.

layers.text: Skin, saphenous plane, fascia, posterior-compartment muscle, extra-periosteal tibia.

structures_at_risk.text: The saphenous vein and nerve, and the deep posterior compartment if fascia is closed, are at risk.

danger_zones.text: Closing deep fascia over the deep posterior space is the compartment-syndrome danger zone.

retraction_hazards.text: Stay extra-periosteal and stop at the posterolateral tibial edge rather than chasing the fibula.

exposure.text: Shows the flat posterior tibia for plating with little contouring, and can also be used for a medial fasciotomy. Access is tibia only, not fibula.

limitations.text: Does not reach the fibula. Use it when only posteromedial skin is safe.

indications.text: Used for open posterior plating when only posteromedial tissues can be incised, and as a medial fasciotomy incision.

closure.text: Almost always leave deep fascia open. Close only skin and subcutaneous tissue.

complications.text: Complications include saphenous injury and deep-posterior compartment syndrome if fascia is closed.

procedure_applications.condition: The posterior tibia is plated because only the posteromedial skin is safe to incise

questions.question: Where is the posteromedial tibial-shaft incision placed?
questions.answer: 1–2 cm posterior to the palpated posteromedial tibial border.

questions.question: How far should dissection go?
questions.answer: Not beyond the posterolateral aspect of the tibia; the middle three-fifths of the posterior tibia can be exposed.

questions.question: Should deep fascia be closed?
questions.answer: Almost never; leave it open to protect the deep posterior compartment.
